new_statements.quote: El acento en mazateco es culminativo, es decir, sus palabras prosódicas cuentan con una sola silaba prominente (Cfr. Kager 2007, p. 196). Su direccionalidad es de izquierda a derecha y recae en la última sílaba. De esta manera las palabras monosilábicas son acentuadas, ya que son una palabra por sí mismas, y las bisilábicas y las trisilábicas se acentúan en la última sílaba, con esto se entiende que las otras sílabas son átonas. [...] es notorio que la segunda sílaba cuenta con una mayor duración que la primera porción, es decir, la sílaba tónica tiene una duración de 152 ms frente 62 ms de la vocal de la sílaba átona.
new_statements.translation: Stress in Mazatec is culminative, i.e. its prosodic words have a single prominent syllable (cf. Kager 2007:196). Its directionality is left to right and it falls on the last syllable. Thus monosyllabic words are stressed, since they are words in themselves, and disyllabic and trisyllabic words are stressed on the last syllable, the other syllables being unstressed. [...] it is noticeable that the second syllable has greater duration than the first portion, i.e. the stressed syllable lasts 152 ms against 62 ms for the vowel of the unstressed syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the final syllable of the prosodic word (words are mono-, di- or trisyllabic; compounds also stress the last syllable, e.g. ko.ˈta 'treinta', ho.ˈko 'sesenta'). Duration is the proposed correlate (F0 and intensity are taken up by lexical tone, 4 levels + contours). The stressed (final) syllable licenses the oral/nasal vowel contrast, morphological contour tones and laryngealized vowels; these contrasts neutralize in unstressed syllables.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; author speculates that final lengthening yields iambic feet but leaves it open.
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress placement; notes the voiceless velar approximant may keep its voice-type contrast in unstressed syllables (p. 148), and that word maximum is three syllables.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the 'palabra prosódica'; examples are citation-form nouns and numeral/noun compounds; Rains 2026 restates it as the last syllable of the morpheme being tonic. Tone language (4 level tones + contours) with an explicit stress statement.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes the Mazatec of San Lorenzo Cuaunecuiltitla (Oaxaca), one of the municipalities Glottolog/ISO assign to Puebla and Northeastern Mazatec (pbm, pueb1234); Rains 2026 (citing Carrera 2025) calls it representative of the Puebla variety because Puebla-side communities were settled from San Lorenzo c. 1900. The Huehuetlán and Ateixtlahuaca varieties within pbm are not covered.

sources.note: Cap. II §2.4 'El acento' (pp. 39-41): stress is culminative, assigned left-to-right, falls on the LAST syllable of the prosodic word; monosyllables stressed, bi- and trisyllables final-stressed (examples no.ˈɲo 'perro', tɨ.ɾɨ.ˈte 'ajolote'); duration is the likely correlate (tonic V 152 ms vs atonic 62 ms), F0/intensity belong to tone; speculates iambic feet; stressed syllable licenses oral/nasal V contrast, contour tones, laryngealization; restated p. 51 and pp. 73-74 (nasality lost in unstressed first member of compounds, e.g. ko.ˈta 'treinta').
